question: The simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2,200 at the rate of 7% per annum in 2 years is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net **Simple Interest** percentage = Rate × Time

Effective **Rate** = 7% × 2 = 14%

**Simple Interest** = 14% of ₹2,200

SI = 14 × 22 = 308

**∴ The correct answer is ₹308.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹2,200

**Rate (R)** = 7% per annum

**Time (T)** = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/481d6b56d5450c6e2419077aa41349f696b80c145e229e0172b95ea652ea400e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (2200 × 7 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 22 × 14

⇒ SI = ₹308

**∴ The correct answer is ₹308.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount

The total sum of money payable at the end of the period is calculated as **Amount = Principal + Simple Interest**.

Compound Interest (CI)

Unlike SI, **Compound Interest** is calculated on the principal and also on the accumulated interest of previous periods. Formula: A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ.

SI vs CI Relationship

For the first year, when interest is compounded annually, the **Simple Interest** is exactly equal to the **Compound Interest**.
